acceptOwnership().details: The new owner accepts the ownership transfer.

create(bytes32,uint256,address,address,a.details: Tokens are always pulled from msg.sender. The refundAddress param controls      who can call refund — useful for coordinators/routers acting on behalf of a user.

params.amount: Token amount to lock (caller must have approved this contract)
params.claimAddress: Address authorized to redeem the locked tokens
params.preimageHash: SHA-256 hash of the secret preimage
params.refundAddress: Address that can refund after timelock (does not have to be msg.sender)
params.timelock: Unix timestamp after which the refund address can reclaim tokens

create(bytes32,uint256,address,address,u.details: Convenience wrapper — uses msg.sender as the sender (refund address)

params.amount: Token amount to lock (caller must have approved this contract)
params.claimAddress: Address authorized to redeem the locked tokens
params.preimageHash: SHA-256 hash of the secret preimage — an indexed event topic,                      not an identifier: swaps may share one, and `key` tells them apart
params.timelock: Unix timestamp after which the sender can reclaim tokens

owner().details: Returns the address of the current owner.

pendingOwner().details: Returns the address of the pending owner.

recoverEther(address).details: No function here is payable, so a balance can only come from a force-send      (selfdestruct, coinbase, or a transfer to the address before deployment). None of      it belongs to a swap, so the full balance is recoverable.

recoverExcessToken(address,address).details: An ERC20 transfer into this contract cannot be refused, so the balance can      exceed `lockedAmounts[token]`. Only that difference is movable: the subtraction      floors at what every active swap is owed, so no call here can reduce the balance      below the amount its settlements will need.

params.token: Token to recover the excess of

redeem(bytes32,uint256,address,address,u.details: Only the designated claimAddress can call this — msg.sender is used as      claimAddress in the key lookup. Tokens are sent to msg.sender.

params.preimage: Secret whose SHA-256 hash matches the preimageHash used at creation
params.timelock: Timelock that was set at creation

redeemBySig(bytes32,uint256,address,addr.details: Anyone can call this function. The claimAddress is recovered from the signature      which includes msg.sender as the authorized caller, destination, sweepToken,      minAmountOut, and callsHash. Tokens are sent to msg.sender (not claimAddress).      All execution parameters are cryptographically bound to the signature, so the      outcome is guaranteed by the signer regardless of who submits the transaction.

params.callsHash: Hash of the calls array (bound to signature, prevents call substitution)
params.destination: Address where the caller intends to route tokens after redeem
params.minAmountOut: Minimum amount of sweepToken required (bound to signature)
params.preimage: Secret whose SHA-256 hash matches the preimageHash used at creation
params.sweepToken: Token the caller will sweep to destination (bound to signature)
params.timelock: Timelock that was set at creation

returns.claimAddress: The address recovered from the signature

refund(bytes32,uint256,address,address,u.details: Convenience wrapper — tokens are sent back to msg.sender

params.claimAddress: Claim address that was set at creation
params.preimageHash: The preimage hash used at creation
params.timelock: Timelock that was set at creation

refund(bytes32,uint256,address,address,u.details: msg.sender must still be the original sender (enforced via the hash).      Useful for sending tokens to a coordinator/router for further processing.

params.claimAddress: Claim address that was set at creation
params.destination: Address to receive the refunded tokens
params.preimageHash: The preimage hash used at creation
params.timelock: Timelock that was set at creation

refundBySig(bytes32,uint256,address,uint.details: Collaborative refund. Both parties consent — the sender by being msg.sender      (exactly as in `refund`), the claimAddress by an EIP-712 signature over the      swap terms with `sender = msg.sender`. The signature only waives the timelock;      it moves nothing on its own. A claimAddress that signs and then calls with      itself as sender addresses a key it never funded, so it cannot route the      locked tokens to itself. Tokens go to msg.sender.      No expiry on the signature, on purpose: it is bound to one key, and that key      can leave Active exactly once, so every signature over it dies with the first      settlement that lands.

params.preimageHash: The preimage hash used at creation (not the preimage — the                     sender does not know it)
params.timelock: Timelock that was set at creation

returns.claimAddress: The address recovered from the signature

refundFor(bytes32,uint256,address,addres.details: Permissionless: anyone may call once the timelock has passed, and the only      thing the caller decides is to pay the gas. The key names `sender`, and the      tokens can only go there, so a wrong `sender` addresses a swap that does not      exist rather than redirecting one that does. Lets a service sweep expired      locks back to depositors who cannot submit a transaction themselves.

params.claimAddress: Claim address that was set at creation
params.preimageHash: The preimage hash used at creation
params.sender: Sender (refund address) that was set at creation; receives the tokens
params.timelock: Timelock that was set at creation

rehash(bytes32,uint256,address,uint256,b.details: Collaborative rehash, consented to exactly like `refundBySig`: the sender by      being msg.sender, the claimAddress by an EIP-712 signature over the old terms      (with `sender = msg.sender`) and the new ones. Lets a swap whose far side      failed (an unpayable Lightning invoice, say) be retried under a fresh hash      without unwinding the lock. Nothing is transferred and `lockedAmounts` does      not move: the old key becomes Rehashed and the new key Active, with the same      amount, token, sender and claimAddress.      The new timelock must lie in the future, as at creation, and must not be      shorter than the current one: a rehash never shortens the timelock, so the      claimAddress keeps at least the claim window it was promised, whatever it      signed. Equal or later is accepted.      No `SwapCreated` fires for the new key — consumers follow `SwapRehashed`.      The new key is taken on a first-come basis like any other: a third party who      learns the agreed terms can `create` under them first and make this call      revert with `SwapExists`. That costs them a lock the claimAddress may redeem      and leaves the original untouched, so the parties simply agree on fresh terms.

params.newPreimageHash: Preimage hash the lock continues under
params.preimageHash: The preimage hash used at creation
params.timelock: Timelock that was set at creation

returns.claimAddress: The address recovered from the signature
returns.newKey: The key the lock continues under

renounceOwnership().details: Disabled: recovery is owner-gated, so an ownerless contract could never release      a mis-sent balance again. Use `transferOwnership` / `acceptOwnership` instead.

params.key: The swap key (see `computeKey`, or the `key` field of `SwapCreated`)

transferOwnership(address).details: Starts the ownership transfer of the contract to a new account. Replaces the pending transfer if there is one. Can only be called by the current owner. Setting `newOwner` to the zero address is allowed; this can be used to cancel an initiated ownership transfer.
